arxiv-2011-02453.title: Failure Probability Constrained AC Optimal Power Flow
arxiv-2011-02453.creator: Anirudh Subramanyam, Jacob Roth, Albert Lam, and Mihai Anitescu
arxiv-2011-02453.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Anirudh Subramanyam, Jacob Roth, Albert Lam, and Mihai Anitescu. Despite cascading failures being the central cause of blackouts in power transmission systems, existing operational and planning decisions are made largely by ignoring their underlying cascade potential. This paper posits a reliability-aware AC Optimal Power Flow formulation that seeks to design a dispatch point which has a low operator-specified likelihood of triggering a cascade starting from any single component outage.

arxiv-2012-01068.title: Reduced-Order Models for Coupled Dynamical Systems: Data-driven Methods and the Koopman Operator
arxiv-2012-01068.creator: Manuel Santos Gutiérrez, Valerio Lucarini, Mickaël D. Chekroun, Michael Ghil
arxiv-2012-01068.description: Abstract Providing efficient and accurate parametrizations for model reduction is a key goal in many areas of science and technology. Here we present a strong link between data-driven and theoretical approaches to achieving this goal. Formal perturbation expansions of the Koopman operator allow us to derive general stochastic parametrizations of weakly coupled dynamical systems.

arxiv-2304-03954.title: Quantum dynamics as a pseudo-density matrix
arxiv-2304-03954.creator: James Fullwood
arxiv-2304-03954.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by James Fullwood. While in relativity theory space evolves over time into a single entity known as spacetime, quantum theory lacks a standard notion of how to encapsulate the dynamical evolution of a quantum state into a single "state over time".

arxiv-2406-06769.title: DiscoveryWorld : A Virtual Environment for Developing and Evaluating Automated Scientific Discovery Agents
arxiv-2406-06769.creator: Peter Jansen *‡, Marc-Alexandre Côté †, Tushar Khot * Erin Bransom *, Bhavana Dalvi Mishra *
arxiv-2406-06769.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Peter Jansen *‡, Marc-Alexandre Côté †, Tushar Khot * Erin Bransom *, Bhavana Dalvi Mishra *. Automated scientific discovery promises to accelerate progress across scientific domains. However, developing and evaluating an AI agent’s capacity for end-to-end scientific reasoning is challenging as running real-world experiments is often prohibitively expensive or infeasible. In this work we introduce DiscoveryWorld , the first virtual environment for developing and benchmarking an agent’s ability to perform complete cycles of novel scientific discovery.

arxiv-2407-03846.title: Google Topics as a way out of the cookie dilemma?
arxiv-2407-03846.creator: Marius Köppel, Jan-Philipp Muttach (né Stroscher), Gerrit Hornung
arxiv-2407-03846.description: Abstract The paper discusses the legal requirements and implications of the processing of information and personal data for advertising purposes, particularly in the light of the ”Planet49” decision of the European Court of Justice (ECJ) and the ”Cookie Consent II” decision by the German Federal Court (Bundesgerichtshof, BGH).

arxiv-2408-10687.title: Structure of optimal gradient flows bifurcations on closed surfaces
arxiv-2408-10687.creator: Illia Ovtsynov, Alexandr Prishlyak
arxiv-2408-10687.description: Abstract We consider structure of typical gradient flows bifurcations on closed surfaces with minimal number of singular points. There are two type of such bifurcations: saddle-node (SN) and saddle connections (SC). The structure of a bifurcation is determinated by codimension one flow in the moment of bifurcation.

arxiv-2410-22375.title: Rethinking Code Refinement: Learning to Judge Code Efficiency
arxiv-2410-22375.creator: Minju Seo Jinheon Baek Sung Ju Hwang, KAIST, DeepAuto
arxiv-2410-22375.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated impressive capabilities in understanding and generating codes. Due to these capabilities, many recent methods are proposed to automatically refine the codes with LLMs. However, we should rethink that the refined codes (from LLMs and even humans) are not always more efficient than their original versions.

arxiv-2506-07341.title: Slow and Fast Neurons Cooperate in Contextual Working Memory through Timescale Diversity
arxiv-2506-07341.creator: Tomoki Kurikawa
arxiv-2506-07341.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Tomoki Kurikawa. Neural systems process information across a broad range of intrinsic timescales, both within and across cortical areas. While such diversity is a hallmark of biological networks, its computational role in nonlinear information processing remains elusive. In this study, we examine how heterogeneity in intrinsic neural timescales within the frontal cortex—a region central to cognitive control—enhances performance in a context-dependent working memory task.

arxiv-2506-14837.title: Improved Iterative Refinement for Chart-to-Code Generation via Structured Instruction
arxiv-2506-14837.creator: Chengzhi Xu, Yuyang Wang, Lai Wei, Lichao Sun, Weiran Huang, [0.1cm] MIFA Lab, Shanghai Jiao Tong University
arxiv-2506-14837.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Chengzhi Xu, Yuyang Wang, Lai Wei, Lichao Sun, Weiran Huang, [0.1cm] MIFA Lab, Shanghai Jiao Tong University. Recently, multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have attracted increasing research attention due to their powerful visual understanding capabilities. While they have achieved impressive results on various vision tasks, their performance on chart-to-code generation remains suboptimal. This task requires MLLMs to generate executable code that can reproduce a given chart, demanding not only precise visual understanding but also accurate translation of visual elements into structured code.

arxiv-2506-19823.title: Persona Features Control Emergent Misalignment
arxiv-2506-19823.creator: Miles Wang, Tom Dupré la Tour, Olivia Watkins, Alex Makelov, Ryan A. Chi, Samuel Miserendino, Johannes Heidecke, Tejal Patwardhan, Dan Mossing, OpenAI
arxiv-2506-19823.description: Abstract Understanding how language models generalize behaviors from their training to a broader deployment distribution is an important problem in AI safety. Betley et al. 2025b discovered that fine-tuning GPT-4o on intentionally insecure code causes “emergent misalignment,” where models give stereotypically malicious responses to unrelated prompts.

arxiv-2511-15474.title: Batalin-Fradkin-Vilkovisky Quantization of Quadratic Gravity
arxiv-2511-15474.creator: Jorge Bellorin
arxiv-2511-15474.description: Abstract 1 Introduction The Hamiltonian is a necessary ingredient in any quantum system. It is the operator that determines the time evolution, according to the postulates of quantum mechanics. Additionally, the process of canonical quantization is based on the existence of conjugated pairs that satisfy canonical commutation relations.

pmc-11338128.title: Pulmonary arterial compliance as a measure of right ventricular loading in mitral regurgitation
pmc-11338128.creator: Hannah Kempton, Sara Hungerford, David W. Muller, Christopher S. Hayward
pmc-11338128.description:
A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Graphical abstract

Background

Left heart failure is the most common cause of pulmonary hypertension (PH), complicating an estimated 60 to 70 % of cases [1], [2]. Left heart failure is frequently associated with valvular heart disease, and mitral regurgitation (MR) is the most commonly encountered valve lesion [3], in which the development of pH and right heart failure are important determinants of prognosis [4], [5], [6], [7], [8], [9], [10].

pmc-12374970.creator: Adele Alagia, Kamal Ajit, Arianna Di Fazio, Qilin Long, Monika Gullerova
pmc-12374970.description: DNA integrity is constantly challenged by both endogenous and exogenous damaging agents, resulting in various forms of damage. Double-strand breaks (DSBs) represent a particularly severe form of damage, due to the physical separation of DNA strands.

pmc-13194074.title: Laparoscopic extraperitoneal techniques in ventral hernia repair: a retrospective comparative study of TAPP and TEP
pmc-13194074.creator: R. Croceri, A. Tek, L. Aragone, J. P. Medina, D. E. Pirchi
pmc-13194074.description: BackgroundVentral hernia repair has traditionally been performed laparoscopically using the intraperitoneal onlay mesh (IPOM) technique, which is simple and widely available but carries the drawback of mesh–viscera contact. Extraperitoneal approaches such as transabdominal preperitoneal (TAPP) and totally extraperitoneal (TEP) repair have emerged as alternatives that avoid this limitation, allowing the use of standard meshes without fixation.

pmc-13371253.title: Causal effects of oral microbiome traits on female reproductive diseases: a two-sample Mendelian randomization study
pmc-13371253.creator: Xiuye Xing, Wenjia Meng, Weiwei Chen, Xinlei Shi, Dachao Wei, Qun Lu
pmc-13371253.description: ObjectiveFemale reproductive diseases (FRDs) impose a substantial health burden. We used two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR) to evaluate potential causal effects of genetically predicted oral microbiome traits on FRDs.

pmc-13530263.title: Targeting individual pain catastrophizing to reduce migraine-related disability: a randomized controlled proof-of-concept trial using an online CBT intervention
pmc-13530263.creator: Janosch Fox, Charly Gaul, Nicolina Laura Peperkorn, Julia Ohse, Joshua Krutzki, Jona Körber, Youssef Shiban
pmc-13530263.description: This mechanistic randomized controlled proof-of-concept trial (RCT) investigated whether a brief online Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT)-based avatar intervention can reduce individual pain catastrophizing in individuals with migraine and examined whether reductions in individual pain catastrophizing are associated with decreased migraine-related disability. Migraine is a highly disabling disorder, yet the mechanisms underlying migraine-related disability remain poorly understood.
